memos.scout:
The honest case for buying is weak, and I can't make it without overstating the data.

The strongest point is volume: about $457K traded in the last 15 minutes, with 941 buyers. That's real activity, and the coin is up 31.6% over 30 minutes. But the same window shows net flow of -5.7 SOL, with sellers (914) almost matching buyers and sell SOL (1945) nearly equal to buy SOL (1939). That's churn, not accumulation.

The curve data points the other way. Bundle share is 1.0, meaning every early buy came through bundled transactions, and the top 3 wallets hold 70% of early flow. The 2-minute post-graduation sell-to-buy ratio is 0.93, and a launch bot was present. The coin is already down 74.6% from its 30-minute high, with a -53% return over the last 15 minutes. Demand that is still here in 30-60 minutes would show stabilization, and nothing in the brief shows that.

Verdict: no case to buy. Coordinated early buying, heavy sell-side pressure, and an ongoing drawdown all fit the pattern that loses money on this desk. Skip.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: a late exit into distribution after the spike has already retraced. The coin is 74.6% off its 30-minute high and down 53% over the last 15 minutes, yet still shows 941 buyers versus 914 sellers and sells outpacing buys (sell_sol 1945 vs buy_sol 1939). Net flow is flat-to-negative while volume is $457k, which points to churn and exit liquidity rather than new demand. Curve data is concerning: bundle_share is 1.0 and top3_share is 0.70, consistent with coordinated early buying and a completer taking 68% of the curve. The launch bot and 0.93 sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes add to the insider-distribution read. With a 104 SOL pool, a $20 round trip faces 1.4-5.1% costs before any further dip. Skip.
